slides.title: Joining loans to readable labels
body: Unit 2 · Week 5 · Lesson 1
Match primary and foreign keys to explain an active-loan report.
slides.notes: Use the separate database-project.sqlite edition of the equipment desk. ReplacementCost contains fictional whole-dollar teaching estimates, not current prices. Activities are ungraded. This week practices joins and summaries; controlled changes follow in Week 6. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: A report needs facts from several tables
body: Loan stores BorrowerID and EquipmentID.
Borrower stores the borrower’s label.
Equipment stores the item’s description.
slides.notes: Recall that each Loan row is one borrowing event. BorrowerID and EquipmentID are FKs. The result should show readable labels without copying them into stored Loan rows. Introduce the separate project database and its cost field; retain four Borrower, three Category, five Equipment and six Loan rows. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: One loan, two key matches
slides.notes: Trace L001 by hand before showing SQL. The ON conditions must match corresponding identifiers. EquipmentDescription is unsuitable for identifying a physical item because E01 and E04 are both Camera. A join creates a query result without merging the stored tables. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: A readable active-loan query
body: l, b and e are short table labels called aliases.
slides.notes: An alias qualifies the source of a field: l.BorrowerID belongs to Loan labelled l. INNER JOIN keeps matching rows. ON supplies the key match. The four active events are L001, L006, L002, L004 in due-date order. DueDate can determine ordering without appearing in this selected result. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.
slides.code:
SELECT l.LoanID, b.BorrowerLabel, e.EquipmentDescription
FROM Loan AS l
INNER JOIN Borrower AS b ON l.BorrowerID = b.BorrowerID
INNER JOIN Equipment AS e ON l.EquipmentID = e.EquipmentID
WHERE l.Returned = 0
ORDER BY l.DueDate, l.LoanID;

slides.title: The complete active-loan result
slides.notes: These are four event rows, not a count of distinct descriptions. L001 and L004 have different item/borrower keys even though their descriptions match. The query reads l.DueDate for ordering. Compare all returned rows with the source records, not just the row count. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: A join to explain independently
body: Trace L002 through the borrower and item keys.
Run the worked join and identify its row for L002.
Explain the purpose of each ON condition.
slides.notes: Use workbook question 1 for the key trace. L002 links to B002 Learner B and E02 Tripod, with due date 2026-04-08 and Returned=0. Learners should name both source and target fields. Optional support: follow L001 again, then explain L002 without the model. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: The tables stay separate
body: Does INNER JOIN copy BorrowerLabel into the stored Loan table?
Explain where the value comes from when the query runs.
slides.notes: No. The DBMS matches Loan.BorrowerID to Borrower.BorrowerID and reads BorrowerLabel for the result. The stored relational structure remains separate. Later changing a label changes the managed borrower fact rather than every loan event. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: A new loan, an existing borrower
body: A borrower takes another item in a later loan event.
Explain which identifier is new and which reference can repeat.
slides.notes: A distinct LoanID identifies the new event. BorrowerID can repeat across Loan rows, as can EquipmentID across history. A new current loan still needs valid references and a separate availability/overlap check. Do not remove legitimate repeated references. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: Loan history and category joins
body: Unit 2 · Week 5 · Lesson 2
Follow item keys to categories and diagnose incorrect matches.
slides.notes: Use the separate database-project.sqlite edition of the equipment desk. ReplacementCost contains fictional whole-dollar teaching estimates, not current prices. Activities are ungraded. This week practices joins and summaries; controlled changes follow in Week 6. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: A third key match
body: Equipment E01 stores CategoryID C01.
Which table supplies the category name Imaging?
slides.notes: Category supplies CategoryName through CategoryID. Recall the Loan to Equipment match first, then Equipment to Category. Category belongs to the item, not directly to a borrower. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: A category history query
body: Each output row still represents one loan event.
slides.notes: The complete report has six rows: L001/E01/Imaging; L002/E02/Support; L003/E03/Audio; L004/E04/Imaging; L005/E02/Support; L006/E05/Audio. There is no Returned filter, so both active and returned history appears. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.
slides.code:
SELECT l.LoanID, e.EquipmentID, c.CategoryName
FROM Loan AS l
INNER JOIN Equipment AS e ON l.EquipmentID = e.EquipmentID
INNER JOIN Category AS c ON e.CategoryID = c.CategoryID
ORDER BY l.LoanID;

slides.title: A history extract to inspect
slides.notes: This is an extract from the six-row report, not the whole result. L002 and L005 both refer to E02 but represent different events and statuses. A one-to-many join can legitimately repeat an item’s values. Learners should preserve both history rows. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: Three questions for a join
body: Which fields does ON match?
What does one result row represent?
Which rows can INNER JOIN leave out?
slides.notes: ON must match Loan.EquipmentID to Equipment.EquipmentID and Equipment.CategoryID to Category.CategoryID. Result grain is a loan event. INNER JOIN omits rows lacking a match. Correct required FKs protect the supplied relationships when enforced. The join does not automatically report parent rows with no child events. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: A readable history report
body: Trace L003 through its borrower, item and category.
Predict the six category-history rows, then run the query.
Explain why matching descriptions would be unreliable.
slides.notes: L003 links to B001 Learner A, E03 Recorder and C03 Audio. Compare all six rows in the worked report file. E01 and E04 share Camera as a description, so descriptions cannot uniquely identify an item. Missing ON conditions can combine unrelated rows. Repair the key match rather than adding DISTINCT to hide a problem. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: An unused borrower
body: Imagine a valid borrower with no loan events.
Would an inner-joined loan report include that borrower?
slides.notes: No. With no matching Loan row, the borrower has no result row. This can be reasoned through without inserting data this week. A report including every borrower, even with zero loans, requires a different query design. Do not invent a loan to make the borrower appear. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: A suspicious row count
body: A six-event history query returns many more than six rows.
Which join conditions would you inspect first?
slides.notes: Inspect missing or incorrect ON conditions and non-unique description matches. For the supplied six loans, unique referenced item/category keys give one matching item and category per loan. Repeated IDs across legitimate loan events are expected; unrelated combinations are not. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: Inventory summaries with aggregates
body: Unit 2 · Week 5 · Lesson 3
Calculate summaries from rows that represent the right thing.
slides.notes: Use the separate database-project.sqlite edition of the equipment desk. ReplacementCost contains fictional whole-dollar teaching estimates, not current prices. Activities are ungraded. This week practices joins and summaries; controlled changes follow in Week 6. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: What one input row represents
body: For inventory value, should you start from Equipment or Loan?
Explain what each table counts once.
slides.notes: Equipment has one row per physical item. Loan has one row per event, so E02 occurs twice in its history. Starting with joined history can duplicate the cost for E02 or omit unused items. Choose input rows to match the question. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: Fictional replacement estimates
slides.notes: These are fixed fictional teaching values, not market prices. Five items total 1400. Mean 280, minimum 80 and maximum 600. Ask learners to calculate by hand before SQL. ReplacementCost is added in database-project.sqlite, not the previous SQL-basics starter. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: An inventory summary
body: Predict the five summary values before running.
slides.notes: The complete single-row result is 5, 1400, 280.0, 80, 600. Each aggregate summarises the Equipment input rows. AS gives readable result headings. Numeric summaries should use meaningful numeric attributes, not arbitrary identifiers. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.
slides.code:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS ItemCount,
SUM(ReplacementCost) AS TotalCost,
AVG(ReplacementCost) AS MeanCost,
MIN(ReplacementCost) AS LowestCost,
MAX(ReplacementCost) AS HighestCost
FROM Equipment;

slides.title: The five summary values
slides.notes: Costs are whole-dollar estimates; the sum, mean, minimum and maximum carry dollar units. COUNT(*) is a row count. COUNT(field) counts non-NULL values of that field. SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX ignore NULL input values. Do not confuse a row count with a distinct item count after a join. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: A summary with evidence
body: Complete workbook question 3 and compare with your hand calculation.
Explain why summing costs across loan history changes the question.
Try the empty category C99 from question 10.
slides.notes: Joined loan history has six rows and counts E02 cost 80 twice in the supplied data, yielding 1480 rather than inventory total 1400. For ungrouped aggregates over empty C99 input, expect one row: COUNT(*) 0, other four aggregates NULL. NULL is not automatically zero. A GROUP BY query with no input groups returns no rows. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: Zero rows and a NULL sum
body: No item matches category C99.
Why can COUNT(*) be 0 while SUM(ReplacementCost) is NULL?
slides.notes: COUNT counts zero input rows. SQLite SUM returns NULL when there are no non-NULL inputs. An ungrouped aggregate query still returns one summary row. Do not label NULL as a measured zero cost. The distinction affects how a report communicates missing or absent values. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: A repeated cost is not a repeated item
body: Two different items could have the same replacement estimate.
Would SUM(DISTINCT ReplacementCost) always fix a bad inventory join?
slides.notes: No. It removes repeated numeric values, which might belong to different real items. Correct the input rows and relationships instead. Compute inventory from Equipment, where each physical item is represented once. A repair must preserve two distinct items even if they have equal costs. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

slides.title: Core SQL reports and optional extensions
body: Unit 2 · Week 5 · Lesson 4
Core: a taught join and all five whole-result aggregates.
Optional: grouped summaries and four-table transfer.
slides.notes: Use database-project.sqlite, a fresh working copy of the project edition. Core: workbook Q2a and Q3; optional extension: Q2b and Q4. body: Q2a: show active LoanID, EquipmentID and description.
Match Loan.EquipmentID to Equipment.EquipmentID.
Sort by DueDate, then LoanID; keep one row per loan.
slides.notes: Use database-project.sqlite, a fresh working copy of the project edition. Core: workbook Q2a and Q3; optional extension: Q2b and Q4. body: Complete Q2a and Q3 before revealing the answers.
Predict rows, values and ordering; then run both queries.
Explain one mismatch and retry with changed input.
slides.notes: Use database-project.sqlite, a fresh working copy of the project edition. Core: workbook Q2a and Q3; optional extension: Q2b and Q4. Extension success is not a core checkpoint or an added assessment requirement. Teach a retained extension before any locally issued assessment includes it. A changed core retry filters Equipment to C01: count 2, sum 1050, mean 525, min 450, max 600. The core exit does not require either optional extension. slides.title: Optional extension: group by category
body: Continue only after the core; otherwise retry Q2a/Q3.
slides.notes: Use database-project.sqlite, a fresh working copy of the project edition. Core: workbook Q2a and Q3; optional extension: Q2b and Q4. Extension success is not a core checkpoint or an added assessment requirement. Teach a retained extension before any locally issued assessment includes it. Year 11 inner joins and all five aggregates remain core; the syllabus sets no maximum join count. This lesson limits independent join depth for pacing. Source: https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0020/1232507/Computer-Science-ATAR-Year-11-Syllabus-for-teaching-from-2026.PDF printed p18. Q4 is optional supporting extension for this Year 11 lesson. Explain how GROUP BY forms one aggregate result per represented category. Every selected non-aggregate field is grouped. Inner join omits categories with no items. Expected C01 Imaging 2 1050; C02 Support 1 80; C03 Audio 2 270. Year 12 pathway Step 10 develops grouping. Do not treat this result as a compulsory core achievement.
slides.code:
SELECT c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName, COUNT(*) AS Items,
SUM(e.ReplacementCost) AS TotalCost
FROM Category AS c
INNER JOIN Equipment AS e ON c.CategoryID = e.CategoryID
GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName
ORDER BY c.CategoryID;

slides.title: Optional extension: check grouped totals
slides.notes: Use database-project.sqlite, a fresh working copy of the project edition. Core: workbook Q2a and Q3; optional extension: Q2b and Q4. Extension success is not a core checkpoint or an added assessment requirement. Teach a retained extension before any locally issued assessment includes it. Year 11 inner joins and all five aggregates remain core; the syllabus sets no maximum join count. This lesson limits independent join depth for pacing. Source: https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0020/1232507/Computer-Science-ATAR-Year-11-Syllabus-for-teaching-from-2026.PDF printed p18. Q4 grouped counts sum to 5 and totals to 1400, matching the core inventory result. Optional Q2b adds borrower and category labels through a four-table join; full SQL and all four expected rows are in the explained answers. It extends independent join depth for this lesson, not a syllabus prohibition on four-table queries. Do not add it to core completion criteria or compulsory homework. If time is short, defer it; Year 12 pathway Step 09 provides four-table teaching.

slides.title: Core exit: explain a fresh result
body: Costs 10 and 15: predict COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX.
Why can loan history give the wrong inventory total?
Optional extension success is not needed for this check.
